channel.title: Aditya Singh essays
channel.description: Enterprise AI and agent architecture essays.

item.title: Your AI Agent Needs a Real Kill Switch
item.description: A technical and operating blueprint for reliably stopping an enterprise AI agent's authority and effects across identity, workers, networks, tools, queues, ambiguous transactions, incident evidence, and governed recovery.

item.title: Model Routing Is Capital Allocation
item.description: A production blueprint for routing enterprise AI actions across model, context, tool, retry, and verification portfolios using constrained utility, calibration, novelty controls, counterfactual evaluation, and business-effect SLOs.

item.title: Your Multi-Agent System Is a Distributed System
item.description: A production blueprint for coordinating AI agents with durable workflows, invariants, message contracts, idempotency, fencing, causal ordering, sagas, chaos tests, and business-effect SLOs.

item.title: Human Approval Is a Queueing System
item.description: Treat human-in-the-loop approval as a risk-priced decision service with queueing models, skilled routing, evidence packets, separation of duties, calibration, and operating SLOs.

item.title: Every AI Agent Action Needs a Receipt
item.description: A production architecture for canonical, signed, idempotent, independently verified AI-agent action receipts with lineage, selective disclosure, and recovery.

item.title: Your AI Agent's Memory Is a Database, Not a Prompt
item.description: Treat agent memory as governed enterprise data: versioned, provenance-complete, bitemporal, policy-filtered, poisoning-resistant, and demonstrably deletable.

item.title: Your AI Agent Should Not Have a Standing Role
item.description: Replace standing AI-agent authority with transaction-bound permission leases using proof-bound tokens, one-use execution, verification, and recovery.

item.title: A $2.4M Account Is Escalating. Should the AI Agent Act?
item.description: A practical production architecture for governing consequential CRM agent actions with evidence, action-level risk, human approval, leased permissions, verification, and recovery.

item.title: AI Agent Identity Is Not Enough
item.description: Learn how to control AI agent access with delegated authority, scoped credentials, policy decisions, and audit receipts across five enterprise use cases.

item.title: What an Agent Actually Costs
item.description: Model inference is only part of the bill. See where production AI agent costs accumulate across governance, integration, people, and operations.

item.title: The Enterprise Agent Control Tower: A Production Architecture
item.description: A production blueprint for governing enterprise AI agents across identity, policy, verified outcomes, risk accounting, audit, and containment at scale.

item.title: How to Build an Agentic CRM: A Reference Architecture
item.description: A practical reference architecture for agentic CRM, covering trusted context, durable orchestration, policy controls, human approval, and evaluation.

item.title: Why Traditional CRM Will Die Without Agentic AI
item.description: Static CRM records customer activity but rarely coordinates action. Learn how agentic AI turns it into a governed execution system for modern operations.
